titel: Tyrolean Cuisine – More Than Just Kaiserschmarrn
teaser: From the alpine meadows to fine dining: Tirol’s culinary diversity delights with tradition and innovation.
inhalt:
The **Tirol** cuisine has far more to offer than its famous classics. Regional products, creative chefs, and ancient traditions make it a culinary hotspot.

## Classics

**Kaiserschmarrn** – The torn pancake with Zwetschkenröster.
**Tiroler Gröstl** – Fried potatoes with bacon and onions, served with a fried egg.
**Knödel** – In all variations: Speck-, Spinat-, Käse-, or Grammelknödel.

## Modern Cuisine

More and more top chefs are reinterpreting the **Tirol** cuisine. The restaurant **St. Antoner Hof** (2 toques) and **Sennhütte [Kitzbühel](/orte/kitzbuehel/)** (1 Michelin star) show how traditional and modern flavors can come together.

## Products

- **Tiroler Bergkäse** – Protected designation of origin
- **Speck** – Air-dried and aromatic
- **Almbutter** – Creamy and golden-yellow

## Wine

Even if **Tirol** isn’t the most famous wine region—South **Tirol** wines and local spirits are world-class.

bilder.alt: Tiroler Kulinarik – Mehr als nur Kaiserschmarrn
